    - text: This series of maps combines the Mid-Region Metropolitan Planning Organization (MRMPO) Vulnerability Index (sourced from U.S. Census American Community Survey 2016-2020 demographic data), with the Environmental Protection Agency's 2021 EJ Screen 2.0 environmental justice assessment tool, to represent relative exposure levels to six air pollutants known to be hazardous to human health. It is meant to be a tool for assessing the distribution of pollutant hazard exposure within the region, and to inform public decision-making and action supporting more just and equitable outcomes for public health. Click on the map for demographic information for each census tract with scores representing the relative concentration of populations of concern for health vulnerability and environmental justice considerations (use arrows in the upper right of the pop-up to flip between information layers). The size of each dot on the map corresponds to the relative level of risk each census tract's population are exposed to. Controls in the upper right allow you to drop down the map legend; search by address; change the base map; and turn on or off layer visibility. A percentile value gives a measure for comparison relative to others in the region. For example, a .80 percentile means the value for that variable is higher than in 80% of all tracts in the Albuquerque Metro Planning Area (in the case of the Air Pollution Index however, percentile values are calculated relative to all tracts in the State). Note that the EJSCREEN value does not directly indicate nonattainment of the National Ambient Air Quality Standard (NAAQS) because the indicator in EJSCREEN is based on estimates from a combination of modeling and monitoring for a single year, while nonattainment is determined for a large area (often a county) based on three years of monitoring data.
